cards.title: Battle of Marathon
cards.notes: Changed course of Western civilization; origin of the marathon race

cards.title: Battle of Thermopylae
cards.notes: Leonidas held Xerxes for 3 days; became a symbol of heroic sacrifice

cards.title: Battle of Gaugamela
cards.notes: Alexander the Great defeats Darius III; collapse of the Persian Empire

cards.title: Battle of Zama
cards.notes: Scipio Africanus defeats Hannibal; Rome becomes Mediterranean superpower

cards.title: Battle of Hastings
cards.notes: William the Conqueror defeats Harold II; transforms English culture and language

cards.title: Battle of Agincourt
cards.notes: Henry V defeats a much larger French force; immortalized in Shakespeare's Henry V

cards.title: Fall of Constantinople
cards.notes: End of the Byzantine Empire; marks conventional end of the Middle Ages

cards.title: Battle of Lepanto
cards.notes: Last major battle fought entirely by oar-powered galleys; halted Ottoman westward naval expansion

cards.title: Battle of the Spanish Armada
cards.notes: England repels Spanish invasion fleet; shifts power balance in Europe

cards.title: Battle of Blenheim
cards.notes: Duke of Marlborough and Prince Eugene defeat France; prevents French hegemony

cards.title: Battle of Saratoga
cards.notes: Turning point of the Revolution; convinced France to ally with the United States

cards.title: Battle of Trafalgar
cards.notes: Nelson defeats combined Franco-Spanish fleet; Britain secures naval supremacy for a century

cards.title: Battle of Waterloo
cards.notes: Napoleon's final defeat; end of the Napoleonic era

cards.title: Battle of Gettysburg
cards.notes: Bloodiest battle in American history; turning point of the Civil War

cards.title: Battle of the Little Bighorn
cards.notes: Lt. Col. Custer and 268 soldiers killed; largest U.S. defeat in the Indian Wars

cards.title: Battle of Tsushima
cards.notes: Japan annihilates Russian Baltic Fleet; Japan emerges as a world naval power

cards.title: Battle of the Marne (First)
cards.notes: Stopped the German advance; ended the war of movement on the Western Front

cards.title: Battle of Verdun
cards.notes: ~700,000 casualties; one of the longest and most costly battles in history

cards.title: Battle of the Somme
cards.notes: ~1 million casualties; worst day in British military history (July 1: 57,000 casualties)

cards.title: Battle of Stalingrad
cards.notes: ~2 million casualties; decisive turning point of WWII on the Eastern Front

cards.title: Battle of Midway
cards.notes: Japan loses 4 carriers; turning point of the Pacific War

cards.title: Battle of El Alamein (Second)
cards.notes: Montgomery defeats Rommel; Churchill: 'the end of the beginning'

cards.title: D-Day (Normandy Landings)
cards.notes: Largest seaborne invasion in history; opened Western Front in Europe

cards.title: Battle of the Bulge
cards.notes: Germany's last major Western offensive; costly Allied victory

cards.title: Battle of Iwo Jima
cards.notes: Only battle where U.S. Marine casualties exceeded Japanese; iconic flag photo

cards.title: Battle of Inchon
cards.notes: MacArthur's amphibious landing; reversed North Korean advance

cards.title: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
cards.notes: France's decisive defeat; ended French colonial presence in Indochina

cards.title: Battle of the Ia Drang Valley
cards.notes: First major battle between U.S. and NVA; presaged nature of the Vietnam War

cards.title: Six-Day War
cards.notes: Israel triples its territory in 6 days; reshapes Middle Eastern geopolitics

cards.title: Battle of Fallujah (Second)
cards.notes: Largest urban combat by U.S. forces since Hue City, 1968
